task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about the multilingual public-service desk opening at Bellharrow's civic center. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Bellharrow civic center will open a multilingual navigation desk on Oct. 19, 2026, beside its main reception area.
The desk's first staffed languages will be English, Spanish and Somali, with scheduled interpreters rather than every language available at every hour.
Its purpose is to help residents identify the correct city office, understand required documents and arrange appointments.
Desk employees will not decide housing applications, issue permits or give legal advice about an individual's case.
The city approved two coordinator positions and a contracted interpreting budget of $48,000 for the first year.
The coordinators' salaries are funded separately in the civic center staffing budget and are not included in the interpreting allocation.
Residents can visit without an appointment, although a specialist interpreter may need to be booked for a later conversation.
The city will display a weekly language schedule at reception and provide it by telephone.
Service manager Arla Deyn said, "The first question is often not how to complete a form, but which counter should receive it."
A community survey supplied examples of residents visiting several offices for the same inquiry, but it was not designed to estimate a citywide error rate.
The neighborhood language forum asked the city to track unmet requests for languages outside the initial three.
Forum member Iman Varek said, "Publishing the hours matters as much as publishing the list of languages."
Staff will record inquiry topics and requests they cannot meet without retaining copies of a visitor's personal application documents.
The desk will use a side room for conversations that should not take place in the public reception queue.
The city has not promised that using the desk will shorten the processing time of the underlying application.
Existing city departments remain responsible for decisions and for telling applicants what further evidence they need.
The opening follows a six-month planning period involving reception staff and local organizations that already help residents navigate services.
Those organizations will continue operating independently and are not being absorbed into a city-run advice service.
The civic center's original reception window will remain available for routine inquiries in addition to the new desk.
The building's large wall directory is being replaced because its department names no longer match several current office signs.
A review after three months will examine the language schedule, unmet requests and whether visitors reached the relevant department.
The packet includes no results from that review and no commitment to add a particular fourth language.

forbidden_additions: All languages available at all times or a guaranteed fourth language.
Authority to approve applications, legal representation or guaranteed faster processing.
A citywide error rate inferred from the planning survey.
preserve: Navigation assistance distinguished from substantive decisions by city departments.
The practical importance of published interpreter availability and private conversation space.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
